top_stories.title: Fed holds rates at 3.5%–3.75% as three officials dissent in favor of a hike
points: The Federal Reserve (the US central bank that sets interest rates) kept its benchmark rate at 3.5%–3.75%, but three voting members pushed for a hike instead.
Officials cited Middle East energy shocks keeping inflation above the Fed's 2% target as the reason to stay restrictive.
Bitcoin and Ether each rose about 1% following the decision.
The dissent signals the Fed may be in no hurry to cut rates, a headwind for risk assets since higher rates make risk-free savings more attractive than speculative bets.
Fed policy expectations remain a key short-term driver of bitcoin, ether and altcoin prices; upcoming Fed communications and inflation data are the next catalysts.

unique_angles.point: Framed the dissent as a potential regime shift away from the rate-cut consensus that has propped up crypto valuations under low-rate, accommodative policy.
Provided the exact rate range and the immediate ~1% crypto price reaction plus the energy-shock inflation rationale.

items.title: Senators finalize tougher ethics language in the Clarity Act
points: Senators Thom Tillis and Ruben Gallego agreed on new wording for the provision restricting senior officials from holding crypto assets, after Democrats said Trump's earlier version let him avoid real compliance.

Open issues remain on illicit-finance protections, DeFi safeguards (DeFi = decentralized finance, financial apps running on blockchains without intermediaries), and stablecoin reward rules the American Bankers Association wants tightened.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said a vote before the August recess is likely but uncertain; industry expectations have shifted to September.
White House and Democratic sign-off is still needed; Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong called the bill 'one yard line' from passage.

items.title: Sei Network's SIP-5 offers opt-in quantum resistance
points: SIP-5 gives every Sei account an opt-in migration path to quantum-secure cryptography, triggered only if a credible quantum threat to ECDSA signatures (the elliptic-curve math that currently secures blockchain accounts) emerges.
The opt-in design leaves existing account behavior unchanged, avoiding a disruptive mandatory upgrade while guaranteeing a defined escape route.
Sei is developing new post-quantum signature schemes to cut the performance overhead that today's quantum-resistant algorithms impose.

items.title: Robinhood Chain: deposits climb, usage fades
points: TVL (total value locked, the amount of crypto deposited in a network's apps) hit $325M in under a month, but the turnover ratio collapsed from 9.25x to 1.68x — capital arriving faster than it trades.
Daily DEX volume (DEX = decentralized exchange, peer-to-peer token trading via smart contracts) fell 27% week-over-week to $553M, and active accounts dropped 7% to about 275,000.
A 7% APY on USDG via Robinhood Earn looks like the main deposit magnet rather than organic trading demand.
CEO Vlad Tenev's 'memes' comment helped spark a CASHCAT rally of up to 962% during launch week.
Q2 earnings may reveal whether the team pivots to real-world-asset projects or doubles down on memecoins.

items.title: EtherFi card processed $676.3M and paid out $20M in cashback
points: The card handled $676.3M across 8.5M transactions on 93,758 active cards, averaging $79 per purchase.
It pays 2.95% USDC cashback — roughly $20M returned to users — with 0% FX fees on EUR/USD pairs.
Funds stay non-custodial (users keep control of their own keys rather than parking assets with a payment provider), while the low average ticket suggests everyday consumer spending.

items.title: Thailand's SEC files complaint against Bitkub over concealed hack
points: Regulators allege the exchange hid a cyberattack that led to roughly $47–50M in losses.

issues.subject: Three Fed Members Just Voted to Hike Rates

headlines: Three Federal Reserve members called for interest rate hikes, signaling potential shift away from rate cuts and creating headwinds for risk assets including cryptocurrencies.
Fed dissent on rate strategy reflects ongoing inflation concerns and divisions within the central bank about the pace of monetary policy adjustment.
Higher interest rates typically reduce demand for speculative assets like crypto by making risk-free savings more attractive to investors.

sections.title: Fed Rate Hike Calls Signal Policy Shift
points: Three Fed members publicly advocated for raising interest rates, breaking from the recent consensus toward rate cuts that has supported asset prices.
This dissent suggests the Fed remains concerned about inflation persistence and may not be in a hurry to cut rates despite earlier market expectations.
Rate hikes increase the cost of borrowing and reduce speculative investing appetite, typically pressuring cryptocurrencies and other high-risk assets.

sections.title: Implications for Cryptocurrency Markets
points: Crypto assets have benefited from an environment of low rates and accommodative monetary policy; higher rates shift that dynamic unfavorably.
Market expectations around Fed policy are a key driver of short-term price movements in bitcoin, ethereum, and altcoins.
Investors should monitor upcoming Fed communications and economic data releases for signals about whether rate hikes will actually materialize.
